overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by giving insufficiently specific notice of nonunion personnel negotiations on Oct. 7 and Oct. 21, 2014, but not for topics it never discussed in executive session; post-complaint amendments did not cure the defect.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Oct. 7, 2014 agenda's real-property executive session topic did not name or describe the property.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, when a public body does not actually engage in any executive session deliberation, the Open Meeting Law is not violated with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Oct. 7, 2014 agenda's nonunion personnel contract negotiation topic failed to name the employees to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we find the original notices for those meetings were insufficiently specific because they did not identify the nonunion personnel with whom the Board would be negotiating.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Oct. 21, 2014 agenda's nonunion personnel contract negotiation topic failed to identify the personnel to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: This lack of detail violated the Open Meeting Law, because inclusion of this information would not have compromised the executive session purpose.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Nov. 6, 2014 agenda's real-property and nonunion personnel executive session topics lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: A meeting notice must include sufficient detail to tell the public what matters will be discussed; where nothing is discussed, there cannot be insufficient notice of the discussion.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
